title: DPEPO: Diverse Parallel Exploration Policy Optimization for LLM-based Agents

paper.title: DPEPO: Diverse Parallel Exploration Policy Optimization for LLM-based Agents
paper.abstract:
Abstract Large language model (LLM) agents that follow the sequential ‘‘reason-then-act’’ paradigm have achieved superior performance in many complex tasks.
However, these methods suffer from limited exploration and incomplete environmental understanding, as they interact with only a single environment per step.
In this paper, we first introduce a novel paradigm that enables an agent to interact with multiple environments simultaneously and share cross-trajectory experiences.
Building upon this paradigm, we further propose Diverse Parallel Exploration Policy Optimization (DPEPO), a reinforcement learning (RL) algorithm that encourages the agent to perform diverse parallel exploration.
There are two stages in DPEPO: initial supervised fine-tuning (SFT) imparts basic parallel reasoning and action generation, followed by reinforcement learning stage with a hierarchical reward scheme.
We design a parallel trajectory-level success reward and two step-level rewards: Diverse Action Reward and Diverse State Transition Reward, which actively penalize behavioral redundancy and promote broad exploration.
Extensive experiments on ALFWorld and ScienceWorld show that DPEPO achieves state-of-the-art (SOTA) success rates, while maintaining comparable efficiency to strong sequential baselines. 1 1 1 Code is available at https://github.com/LePanda026/Code-for-DPEPO

Learn more × Back to arXiv License: arXiv.org perpetual non-exclusive license arXiv:2604.24320v1 [cs.CL] 27 Apr 2026 DPEPO: Diverse Parallel Exploration Policy Optimization for LLM-based Agents Junshuo Zhang Affiliation: University of Electronic Science and Technology of China Affiliation: DiDi Chengrui Huang Affiliation: University of Electronic Science and Technology of China Affiliation: DiDi Feng Guo Affiliation: University of Electronic Science and Technology of China Zihan Li Affiliation: University of Electronic Science and Technology of China Ke Shi Affiliation: University of Electronic Science and Technology of China Menghua Jiang Affiliation: DiDi Jiguo Yu Affiliation: University of Electronic Science and Technology of China Shuo Shang Affiliation: University of Electronic Science and Technology of China Shen Gao Affiliation: University of Electronic Science and Technology of China Abstract Large language model (LLM) agents that follow the sequential ‘‘reason-then-act’’ paradigm have achieved superior performance in many complex tasks. However, these methods suffer from limited exploration and incomplete environmental understanding, as they interact with only a single environment per step. In this paper, we first introduce a novel paradigm that enables an agent to interact with multiple environments simultaneously and share cross-trajectory experiences. Building upon this paradigm, we further propose Diverse Parallel Exploration Policy Optimization (DPEPO), a reinforcement learning (RL) algorithm that encourages the agent to perform diverse parallel exploration. There are two stages in DPEPO: initial supervised fine-tuning (SFT) imparts basic parallel reasoning and action generation, followed by reinforcement learning stage with a hierarchical reward scheme. We design a parallel trajectory-level success reward and two step-level rewards: Diverse Action Reward and Diverse State Transition Reward, which actively penalize behavioral redundancy and promote broad exploration. Extensive experiments on ALFWorld and ScienceWorld show that DPEPO achieves state-of-the-art (SOTA) success rates, while maintaining comparable efficiency to strong sequential baselines. 1 1 1 Code is available at https://github.com/LePanda026/Code-for-DPEPO 1 Introduction Figure 1: ReAct-based agent constructs environmental understandings from a narrow, linear view. Our DPEPO allows agent to build comprehensive cognition of environments from diverse parallel exploration. LLM-based autonomous agents commonly adopt the ReAct paradigm Yao et al. (2023) , where the agent alternates between reasoning and acting: it selects a single action, observes the environmental feedback, and then uses that observation to inform its next step. This “reason, then act” framework has shown notable success in complex, long-horizon tasks Shridhar et al. (2021) ; Yao et al. (2022) ; Wang et al. (2022) by enabling structured, step-by-step reasoning. Recent work Richens et al. (2025) demonstrates that a comprehensive understanding of the environment is crucial for effective and reliable agents. However, ReAct imposes a fundamental limitation: at each step, the agent can perform only one action and observe a single observation. This restricts the breadth of environmental exploration and forces the agent to construct its understanding from a narrow, linear view. As a result, agents often develop an incomplete and biased cognition of the environment, leading to suboptimal decisions and failures in complex tasks. A straightforward approach to broaden exploration is to sample multiple independent trajectories for the same task. However, this naive multi-sampling strategy faces two critical shortcomings: (1) Lack of diversity : Despite increased output entropy, actions sampled across multiple trials tend to converge to similar choices, failing to promote truly diverse exploration and preventing the agent from developing a comprehensive grasp of the environment. (2) Inefficiency and isolation : Experiences from different trajectories are neither shared nor leveraged, meaning the agent cannot learn from cross-trajectory insights. Moreover, sampling multiple trials sequentially inflates token consumption and running time, making the approach prohibitively costly for practical deployment. To overcome these limitations, we introduce parallel exploration, a paradigm in which an agent interacts with multiple environments simultaneously. This allows the agent to gather diverse observations in parallel, share experiences across environments, and build a more holistic understanding of the environment dynamics. Building on this exploration paradigm, we propose Diverse Parallel Exploration Policy Optimization (DPEPO), a novel reinforcement learning framework that endows agents with structured parallel exploration capabilities. After an initial SFT phase to acquire basic parallel reasoning and action generation skills, the agent is optimized via a hierarchical reward scheme that encourages diverse exploration at both the trajectory and step levels. Specifically, we design a parallel trajectory-level success reward and two novel step-level rewards: Diverse Action Reward and Diverse State Transition Reward, that actively penalize redundant behaviors. These rewards are combined through a group-relative advantage computation to provide multi-granularity learning signals, enabling the agent to explore more broadly while staying focused on task completion. Extensive experiments on ALFWorld and ScienceWorld, demonstrate that DPEPO achieves state-of-the-art success rates across all task splits. Notably, our analysis of trajectory length and token usage reveals that DPEPO achieves efficiency comparable to strong sequential baselines, despite its parallel nature. Our contributions are summarized as follows: ∙ \bullet We propose Diverse Parallel Exploration Policy Optimization (DPEPO), a novel RL framework that pioneers parallel exploration for agents to build holistic environment cognition. ∙ \bullet We design a Parallel Trajectory-level Success Reward to optimize task completion in concurrent multi-environment settings. ∙ \bullet We propose Parallel Step-level Rewards (Diverse Action & State Transition) to penalize redundancy and foster distinct explorations. ∙ \bullet Extensive experiments on ALFWorld and ScienceWorld show DPEPO achieves SOTA performance in terms of success rates while maintaining comparable efficiency with single exploration methods. 2 Related Work LLM as Autonomous Agents LLMs are increasingly being deployed as autonomous agents across a wide range of domains, including code generation Zhang et al. (2024) , web navigation Abuelsaad et al. (2024) , smart device control Zhang and Zhang (2024) ; Gur et al. (2024) ; Liu et al. (2025b) ; Ye et al. (2025) , external tool use Gao et al. (2024) ; Shi et al. (2024) ; Shi et al. (2025) ; Huang et al. (2025) and interactive gaming Shridhar et al. (2021) ; Yao et al. (2022) ; Wang et al. (2022) ; Wang et al. (2023) . Early LLM-based agents typically relied on engineered prompting strategies Wei et al. (2022) to achieve strong performance, such as ReAct Yao et al. (2023) and Reflexion Shinn et al. (2023) . Recent studies has shifted their focus toward fine-tuning LLMs for agent-related tasks using either SFT Song et al. (2024) ; Xi et al. (2024) or RL Feng et al. (2025) ; Zhang et al. (2025) , aiming to develop agents with greater generalization ability and robustness, ultimately resulting in more efficient and resilient behaviors compared to earlier prompt-based methods. Figure 2: Training framework of our proposed Diverse Parallel Exploration Policy Optimization (DPEPO). Reinforcement Learning for LLM-based Agents Reinforcement learning has been recognized as a foundational approach for enabling LLMs to operate as autonomous agents in complex environments. Early work in this domain primarily employed PPO Schulman et al. (2017) , which allowed agents to learn diverse interactive tasks while avoiding the need for expensive imitation data. With the emergence of reinforcement learning with verifiable reward (RLVR) Guo et al. (2025) ; Lambert et al. (2025) and group-based policy optimization Shao et al. (2024) ; Zheng et al. (2025) ; Kool et al. (2019) ; Liu et al. (2025c) , a series of studies have eliminated complex reward model and critic model, instead adopting rule-based reward signals: GiGPO Feng et al. (2025) proposes anchor state groups to estimate the quality of specific steps; RLVMR Zhang et al. (2025) introduces meta-reasoning and corresponding step-level rewards to address inefficient exploration; iStar Liu et al. (2025a) estimates step rewards via the LLM’s intrinsic implicit rewards. However, these methods remain constrained by the sequential ReAct paradigm, which limits their exploration space and maintains a narrow focus on single-path reasoning. In this work, we introduce a novel reinforcement learning algorithm for training agents with more fine-grained reward shaping, drawing from the insight that more diverse and comprehensive exploration, helping agents build a better understanding of environments, thereby enabling them to perform tasks more effectively. 3 Methodology In this section, we first introduce the parallel agent exploration framework, and then we detail the framework for training the LLM-based agent to perform parallel exploration. The overall architecture is shown in Figure 2 . 3.1 Parallel Agent Exploration Formulation Given a task specified by a prompt and a set of K K parallel environments ℰ = { E 1 , E 2 , … , E K } \mathcal{E}=\{E_{1},E_{2},\dots,E_{K}\} sharing the same initial state, an LLM-based agent interacts with ℰ \mathcal{E} over multiple turns until the task is completed or the maximum allowed step T T is reached. Specifically, at step t t , the agent selects a subset of all environments ℰ t ′ \mathcal{E}_{t}^{\prime} . Let | ℰ t ′ | |\mathcal{E}_{t}^{\prime}| denote the number of selected subset, due to the agent dynamically selects environments to interact, | ℰ t ′ | |\mathcal{E}_{t}^{\prime}| can vary at each step. For the selected environments, the agent generates a set of parallel actions A t = { ( E i , a t ) ∣ E i ∈ ℰ t ′ } A_{t}=\{(E_{i},a_{t})\mid E_{i}\in\mathcal{E}_{t}^{\prime}\} , which are executed simultaneously in their respective environments. The agent then observes the resulting states S t = { ( E i , s t ) ∣ E i ∈ ℰ t ′ } S_{t}=\{(E_{i},s_{t})\mid E_{i}\in\mathcal{E}_{t}^{\prime}\} . Consequently, the agent’s full trajectory can be denoted as: τ = { ( S t , A t ) } t = 1 T , \tau=\{(S_{t},A_{t})\big\}_{t=1}^{T}, (1) where the trajectory τ \tau consists a sequence of parallel states and parallel actions. 3.2 Parallel Exploration Capability Cold Start We begin with an SFT-based cold start stage to endow the agent with foundational skills for structured output and parallel exploration. For the SFT training data, we introduce human prior knowledge into its synthetic pipeline. The data synthesis pipeline is two steps: (1) We first manually annotated five ground-truth trajectories. Each trajectory consists of multiple steps, with some key steps containing two or more parallel exploration actions. (2) Based on these trajectories, we employ DeepSeek-V3.2 to annotate trajectories containing parallel exploration behaviors. Finally, the agent is fine-tuned on these annotated trajectories, learning to imitate the parallel exploration patterns.
